newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police raid fortune-tellers in fraud swoop.
newsitem.headline: Italian police raid fortune-tellers in fraud swoop.

text.p: Police are investigating some 50 so-called fortune-tellers for suspected fraud after raids on homes and offices across Italy on Tuesday.
The operation against the self-professed "maghi" or wizards was coordinated by Milan's flying squad after complaints by people who said they had been swindled.
"These maghi can't be much good as they didn't predict being investigated," Lucio Carluccio, head of the flying squad, said.
Police raided 79 apartments used by the maghi to receive clients, 68 of them in Milan and in eight other cities.
Specialists in the field say it is almost impossible to put a figure on the number of sorcerers, exorcists and clairvoyants operating in Italy in a business raking in billions of lire.

The maghi advertise their services widely, in occult magazines and on private television stations, offering not just fortune-telling but magic spells to remove the evil eye, good luck charms and love potions and cures of all sorts.
Police said that possible charges against the 50 ranged from aggravated fraud to abuse of peoples' credulity and, under an old law still on the books, of being charlatans.
Carluccio told reporters that among those being investigated were the exotically named "Wizard of Tutankhamun" and the "Wizard of London".
He said police had seized several voodoo-type dolls in the raids as well as various potions, creams and pills which would be analysed to see if they contained any dangerous substances.
Carluccio appealed for more people claiming to have been cheated by the maghi to come forward.
"It isn't easy to admit you have been swindled but some people have done so and others should follow their example," he said.
